title: Insertion tabs: First qualifying slip
topics: Recursion, sorting, binary search and bits
summary: The input contains two rows: a sorted drawer and query values. For each query, produce the first index whose drawer value is at least that query; use the drawer's length if no such index exists. Return the first value in the derived sequence that is at least k, or -1 if there is none. Return the value, not its index.
descriptionMd:
The archive needs insertion tabs for new labels without disturbing an existing sorted drawer. Luz needs the first qualifying slip while the courier waits at the door. Later matches must not jump ahead in the tray.

The input contains two rows: a sorted drawer and query values. For each query, produce the first index whose drawer value is at least that query; use the drawer's length if no such index exists.

Return the first value in the derived sequence that is at least k, or -1 if there is none. Return the value, not its index.

Implement insertionTabsFirstQualifyingSlip(drawers, k). Use k exactly where specified above.

constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.
Numeric readings lie between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000, subject to the task's shape and ordering rules.
The input has exactly two rows, each containing at most 64 integers.

Target time O(q log(n+1)); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
